Protection Warrior Rotation in 

The rotation for Protection Warrior is fast paced and fun. It has many frequent procs that always keep you on your toes.
We primarily focus on building and spending as much rage as possible to cycle our cooldowns faster.

 

 

 
 React to Shield Slam Procs: Shield slam should alwawys be used if it's ready, this will generate the most rage/threat/damage and keep your rotation flowing smoothly.
 

 

 
 

 
 Avoid Rage Waste: Trying to always keep your rage below the cap so you dont 'waste' any is very important. You can always dump more into Ignore Pain . 
 

 

 
 

 
 Utilize your cooldowns frequently.: Avatar is cast on cooldown, roughly every minute or so. We also have Demoralizing Shout shout which comes up very often. Don't be afraid to use Shield Wall to smooth damage intake where necessary.

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Protection Warrior to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Protection Warrior Major Cooldowns

Protection Warrior has 3 main cooldowns they cycle offensively. Avatar / Demoralizing Shout and Shield Charge . These are all to be used on cooldown as best as possible.

 
 Avatar 

Avatar gives you a multitude of perks and can be changed based on talents, but primary it increases all damage done and generally reduces the cooldown of Thunder Clap.

 
 Demo Shout 

This both reduces the damage mobs deal to you and damage you deal to them alongside generating some rage.

 
 Shield Charge 

Shield Charges grants you Shield Block and stuns the target.

 Protection Warrior Advanced Tips

 
 Always Be Casting 

 This is a classic staple for all specs in WoW, ABC. Always be casting. Your gcd usage is extremely important, if you are missing 10-20% of your total casts just because you aren't mashing fast enough then you are going to be losing a significant amount of damage and rage generation. This all plays into itself, less resources, less cdr, less damage when you need it.
 Your casts don't have to be perfect all the time, just make sure you are actually hitting something instead of mashing buttons that aren't ready yet.
